verdict_text: NO. The merge takes the second task vector against the already-modified base: it computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1 - base)` and then `tmp + λ(ft2 - tmp)`, so the ft2 delta is measured against `tmp`, not against the unmodified base. This violates Required result step 2, which requires `out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X] - base[X]) + λ(ft2[X] - base[X])` with both task vectors taken against the original base. The resulting values differ from the reference by more than a reordering of additions, so the 48 merged tensors will fail the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance. The shared-tensor verification, merged count, and 114-tensor checks are otherwise correctly enforced.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
